source_text:
In parabolam vineae
ΟΜΙΛΙΑ ΙΖʹ. ΕΙΣ ΤΗΝ ΠΑΡΑΒΟΛΗΝ ΤΟΥ ΑΜΠΕΛΩΝΟΣ.
Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ, ὅστις ἐξῆλθεν
ἅμα πρωῒ μισθώσασθαι ἐργάτας εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ. Ἤκουσας, ἀγαπητὲ, τῆς
εὐαγγελικῆς τοῦ Κυρίου παραβολῆς· ἄκουε καὶ τὴν ἑρμηνείαν, ἣν κατὰ δύναμιν
ἐροῦμεν. Οἰκοδεσπότης τοῦ μεγάλου οἴκου, 77.1097 τουτέστιν ὁ δεσπότης Θεός·
οἶκος γὰρ, ὁ κόσμος· ∆εσπότης δὲ αὐτοῦ, ὁ κτίσας αὐτὸν Θεός· ἀμπελὼν αὐτοῦ, ἡ
ἀνθρωπεία φύσις· ἐργάται τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος, ὅσοι διακονούμενοι τῇ σωτηρίᾳ τῶν
ἀνθρώπων ἅγιοι· πρώτη ὥρα ὁ καιρὸς τῶν θεοσεβῶν ἐκείνων τῶν περὶ Ἄβελ καὶ
Ἐνὼχ καὶ Νῶε· πρῶτοι γὰρ οὗτοι θεοσεβεῖς, πρῶτοι οὗτοι ἐργάται τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος.
Νῶε γὰρ ἐφύτευσεν ἀμπελῶνα, νοητῶς νόει· πνευματικοὶ γὰρ οἱ λόγοι· ἕως τρίτης
ὥρας οὗτοι εἰργάζοντο· μετὰ τρίτην ὥραν ὁ καιρὸς τῶν περὶ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Ἰσαὰκ καὶ
Ἰακώβ· καὶ οὗτοι γὰρ ἐργάται τῆς σωτηρίας ἡμῶν, τρεῖς τὸν ἀριθμόν· διὰ τοῦτο καὶ
ἕως ἕκτης ὥρας εἰργάσαντο· ἀπὸ ἕκτης ὥρας τὸ μεσαίτατον τῆς ἡμέρας, ὅτε ὁ ἥλιος
σφοδρότερον καταλάμπει τὴν οἰκουμένην, ὁ χρόνος τοῦ νόμου· ὅτι τῷ ὄντι
thought_title: The parable's allegory: landowner, vineyard, laborers, and the hours
orientation: Cyril opens his homily by quoting the parable and then begins to decode each element: the landowner is God, the vineyard is human nature, and the hours are the ages of salvation history.
pass_a_gloss: The kingdom of the heavens was likened to a man, a landowner, who went out at dawn to hire laborers into his vineyard. You heard, beloved, the gospel parable of the Lord; hear also the interpretation, which we will speak according to our ability. The landowner of the great house, that is, the master God; for the house is the world; and its master is the God who created it; his vineyard is human nature; the laborers of the vineyard are all the saints who serve the salvation of humans; the first hour is the time of those God-fearing men around Abel and Enoch and Noah; for these were the first God-fearing men, these were the first laborers of the vineyard. For Noah planted a vineyard; understand it spiritually; for the words are spiritual; until the third hour these men were working; after the third hour is the time of those around Abraham and Isaac and Jacob; for these also are laborers of our salvation, three in number; for this reason they also worked until the sixth hour; from the sixth hour, the midpoint of the day, when the sun shines more intensely upon the inhabited world, is the time of the law; because truly

choices.why: Glossary requires 'landowner' for the parable's master figure, representing God.
Glossary term for the vineyard representing human nature.
Glossary requires 'laborers' for the saints who serve human salvation.
Keeps the master/servant relation explicit while naming God as the world's lord.
Preserves the imperative force and the adverb's sense of non-literal understanding.
rejected: take it in a spiritual sense

choices.why: Glossary requires 'coming' for Christ's incarnation, though the term appears only at the section's edge.

bible_refs.note: Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ, ὅστις ἐξῆλθεν ἅμα πρωῒ μισθώσασθαι ἐργάτας εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ

pass_b_english: "The kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard" (Matthew 20:1). You have heard, beloved, the Lord's parable from the Gospel; now hear the interpretation that we will offer as best we can. The landowner of the great house—that is, the master God. For the house is the world, and its master is the God who created it. His vineyard is human nature. The laborers of the vineyard are all the saints who serve the salvation of human beings. The first hour is the time of those God-fearing men around Abel, Enoch, and Noah; for these were the first God-fearing men, the first laborers of the vineyard. Noah planted a vineyard—understand it spiritually, for these words are spiritual. They worked until the third hour. After the third hour comes the time of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; these too are laborers for our salvation, three in number, and for that reason they worked until the sixth hour. From the sixth hour, the very middle of the day, when the sun shines more intensely upon the inhabited world, comes the time of the law; for truly

last_rejected.why: Missing article: 'the master God' reads as title+name; Greek has 'the master, God' or 'God the master'—two nouns in apposition.
last_rejected.ruling: ὁ δεσπότης Θεός rendered as 'the master God' conveys apposition adequately; no meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: They worked until the third hour
last_rejected.why: English loses explicit 'these' (οὗτοι), making subject unclear; 'they' could refer to all preceding figures.
last_rejected.fix: These worked until the third hour
last_rejected.ruling: οὗτοι is implicit in 'They'; context makes referent clear. Minor stylistic issue, not major error.
